host.notes: Synthetic clean-speech transport and timing probes only. These are not film or TV accuracy benchmarks.

source.generator: macOS say, Samantha voice, 160 words per minute
source.text: Good evening. This is a timing test for near real time television dubbing. We need every sentence to remain synchronized with the video, even when the viewer pauses or seeks.

billing_derivation.warning: The 22- and 100-minute estimates hold the observed generated/source duration ratio constant. Real content, language pairs, silence and cloning behavior will differ. Input-ASR text output, optional images, retries and free quota are excluded.

derived_findings: A live translated audio track can arrive about 1.3 seconds after session configuration with a fixed provider voice in this clean sample.

The clone-once configuration produced first audio about 2.15 seconds later than the fixed-voice configuration. Because voice, source ASR and cloning changed together, this is a confounded configuration difference rather than an isolated clone penalty.
Both generated outputs were materially longer than the source. Streaming translation alone does not provide source-duration matching for video dubbing.
The integration needs source media timestamps, a user-visible base delay, bounded buffering, seek generations, and duration/drift correction.
evidence_limits: No noisy dialogue, music, overlapping speakers, long-form drift, Android TV device, or provider invoice reconciliation.
Timing includes local connection and network conditions on one research host.
secret_handling: No API key, token, authorization header, workspace ID, raw request capture, or credential value is stored in this receipt.
